messages.subject: Re: Performance within a package
messages.body_plain:
Thanks.  Those ideas gave me some good ideas where to look.  The problem ended up having 'nothing to do with packages ( or environments or objects).'  The case seems I was opening then closing connections over and over again.  In the solution, I ended up just simply keeping one connection per work session (full program run) ( and not re-destroying/recreating my tables over and over again within the same program run.) This new method increased my performance by 40x ( 60 seconds down to 1.5 seconds).

On Tuesday, July 29, 2014 12:41:15 PM UTC-5, Gabor Grothendieck wrote:
> Based on info provided can only guess. sqldf will look through the words in the sql statement and if any of those words name a data frame or file connection in the environment defined by the sqldf envir= argument then it will upload it to sqlite so maybe in the package you have extra objects which match names in the sql statement and objects with those names are not present in the interactive version.  If that were the case then the extra time would be the time to upload these extra objects.  Other possibilities are that you are not really using the same data, you are using indexes in one can and not antoher or that the sql statements are not actually the same.  Another possibility is interactively you are using tcltk but not in the package although i would not have though that that would make such a big difference in time.
>
> On Tuesday, July 22, 2014 8:45:21 AM UTC-4, Andre Mikulec wrote:
> > All,
> >
> > I am using the latest downloadable R and the latest CRAN R).
> >
> > When use a sqldf SQLite query in interactive mode ( in the global environment) I get back 'instantaneous' results.  That is good.
> >
> > When I put my R source code into a function within a package and build the package, then run that function  the same query takes 60 seconds to return results.  This not so good.
> >
> > Is anyone having severe speed problems with sqldf being used inside R package functions?
> >
> > Another thing that I am doing is that when I am using sqldf within a function and within a package I am retrieving 'source table data frames' from the global environment ( that were originally put there with "<<-").  Can this be a problem?
> > I have not tested other combinations though and this "retrieve from the global environment" does not seem that this would be a problem?)
> >
> > Any ideas about the slow performance in a package function problem?  Thanks? Can/should I try to make/do a reproducible problem?
> >
> > Andre Mikulec
> >
